correctness.rationale: For n>=1, a proper colouring of K_(2,n) has pole pair u,v and each independent right colour outside {u,v}. Ordered additive-energy equality for four copies allows exactly 4^3 pole base shifts and 4^3 pole-difference triples (d1,d2,d3), with d4=d1+d2-d3 in H=C4 or V4. Group translations remove base poles, preserving the equation; at each right position the four-colour additive constraint has a count T_H(d). Independence over n positions gives E_H(n)=64 sum_(d1,d2,d3) T_H(d)^n exactly for all n. I independently enumerated all 64 triples via the three freely chosen allowed right colours and the forced fourth, reproducing exact C4 histogram 2:2,4:12,6:30,8:1,10:18,21:1 and V4 histogram 4:18,6:24,8:3,10:18,21:1, matching the 64-row CSV and formula. Subtracting gives E_V4-E_C4=128·2^n(4^n−3·3^n+3·2^n−1), which is a surjection count onto three distinguished colours, zero n=1,2 and positive n>=3. Character orthogonality confirms sum_χ |W(χ)|^4=4^(n+2)E_H(n) for the UNnormalized transform; no missing power of 4. Exact 64-state enumeration is exhaustive, while finite n=1..14 numerical formula comparison is not the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The two natural nonisomorphic additive structures of a four-colour palette are indistinguishable by chromatic counting but are first separated by a concrete global harmonic invariant on the entire natural graph family K_(2,n). The finite 64-state complete classification rigorously produces a sharp n3 threshold and explicit asymptotic decay relative to energy. This is a motivated exact graph/Fourier distinction, not an arbitrary small table.

limitations: Only ordered additive energies and unnormalized fourth Fourier moments for labelled K_(2,n) proper four-colourings, n>=1, no extra edge joining poles; no complete Fourier spectrum, other palettes or arbitrary graphs. Priority search bounded.
